key_insight: In retrospective evaluation, LabARIA’s multi-agent AI flagged laboratory quality issues before 96.4% of documented QC actions, with a median lead time of 5.40 days.
clinical_relevance: Coordinated monitoring could help laboratory teams recognize specimen, analytical quality, and workflow problems earlier, but patient-care benefits remain unproven.
method: Integrated specimen workflow surveillance, internal quality control, and patient-based real-time quality control.
Presented tiered alerts for human review through a dashboard and exploratory chatbot.
Evaluated forecasting with controlled patient-result perturbations and synthetic staffing and inventory data.
evidence_signal: Single-center retrospective evaluation included 177,480 specimen-panel records, 75,103 IQC measurements, and 422 QC actions; adding patient-based monitoring increased action recall from 0.964 to 0.993.
watch_item: Recall against documented actions does not establish alert precision or clinical benefit; prospective validation is needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: LabARIA: A Multi-Agent System for Integrative Analytics in Clinical Laboratories
